key_evidence: Cerebras Systems has never been individually assessed. rotation-state records last_assessed: null, and seven of its eight published dimensions are set to an identical 3.5 — the signature of a bulk-import placeholder rather than of an evidence-based assessment.

The scanner performed an individual tier-1 thematic search covering lawsuits, labour, safety, regulatory and humanitarian signals for the 14 days to 2026-08-11 and found NO compassion-relevant evidence, positive or negative.

Cerebras publishes no human rights policy, no independently audited responsibility reporting, no workforce disaggregation and no community-impact data. Under the evidence hierarchy, absence of practice defaults to the lower anchor.
The entire 22.1-point gap is an evidence-absence gap, NOT a conduct gap. No adverse conduct was found.

THIS IS NOT A DOWNGRADE. Per anti-false-positive screen 3e-bis §5, a published score believed mis-calibrated relative to peers must not be relitigated through a one-off baseline-reset proposal. This is filed as flag-for-review for coordinator-level calibration of the uniform-seed AI-lab placeholders, and NO score change is proposed for application.
The one negative signal located — anonymous employee-forum layoff discussion last updated 2026-07-22 — carries no numbers, no timing and no company confirmation, and was not scored.

evidence.claim: Cerebras Systems filed to go public as an AI chip company in April 2026 and completed its IPO on 14 May 2026, raising $5.55 billion.

An earlier 2024 IPO filing was delayed by a federal review of an investment from Abu Dhabi-based G42 and ultimately withdrawn; Cerebras later obtained CFIUS clearance and G42 no longer appears among its investors.
A dedicated tier-1 thematic search for the 14 days to 2026-08-11 found no compassion-relevant evidence for Cerebras Systems in any direction.

notes: FLAG FOR REVIEW — NOT A DOWNGRADE. No score change is proposed for application. The published 60.9 is a never-assessed uniform-seed placeholder (seven of eight dimensions identical at 3.5). The 22.1-point gap measures disclosure, not conduct: no adverse evidence of any kind was located. Applying a one-off 22-point baseline reset on evidence-absence alone would convert a calibration problem into a conduct finding, which the anti-false-positive screen forbids. Referred for coordinator-level calibration review of uniform-seed placeholders across the ai-labs index (Cerebras 3.5s, Cognition AI 2.5s and comparable entries). rotation-state composite/band/rank left at the PUBLISHED values.
